title: Atiyah–Floer cobordism maps III: usual maps and integral normalization
description: A new paper identifies the usual singular Hopf-link maps with the signed mixed-count comparison, and constructs sphere-positive normalization for every closed connected oriented three-manifold through finite products of geometric counts. The manuscript and source are public with a Zenodo archive. The topology guide distinguishes these results, under their stated inputs, from the remaining nonsingular cap and prescribed relative-spin comparisons.

title: Uniform Hermitian–Einstein spectra with repeated stable factors
description: A new paper determines every small Hermitian–Einstein endomorphism eigenvalue for simple two-step extensions with repeated stable factors, with uniform relative accuracy at arbitrarily separated positive scales. It compares actual metrics with an independently balanced matrix model and gives a fixed rank-five geometric example. The manuscript, source and finite calculations are public, with a Zenodo archive; the Geometry & moduli guide distinguishes this completed stationary result from the remaining flow and higher-step questions.

title: Toric tangent stability: complete census and geometric extensions
description: Two revised papers add a complete exact eightfold census and geometric criteria for tangent stability chambers. The census certifies 64 stable, 692 strictly semistable and 5,525 unstable cases, with every strictly semistable case a product. The chamber paper adds positive spanning without local freeness, a Bott-filtration obstruction and an eight-node Calabi–Yau transition. Both retain their original dates and display a separate version date.

title: When Walls Collide: find the missing wall
description: A new explorer follows one exact quartic example in open FJRW theory. Take two paths, find the correction that makes their operations agree, transport a lattice frame around an annulus, and compare full potentials with the period class that misses their difference. Four experiments and a threshold grid connect the calculations to the papers and their remaining geometric question.

title: At the Wall: how geometry loses rigidity
description: A new explorer links stability chambers, weighted extension graphs, small eigenvalues and metric response. Four experiments follow three vanishing scales, compare trees with cycles, and examine the two-factor flow across a stability wall, with the finite calculations and their geometric scope explained alongside.

title: Universal curve counting across Calabi–Yau transitions
description: Two new papers establish rational universal conifold specialization with a complete compact calculation, and give a compact counterexample to general integrality for scalar local-curve factors. The Calabi–Yau guide introduces the programme and its remaining questions. Both manuscripts, their sources and exact calculations are public, with separate Zenodo archives.

title: Research programmes within the guides
description: The research guides now set out the programmes inside each subject: what the papers establish, the theorem or construction still missing, and why it would matter. New sections cover Atiyah–Floer comparisons, open FJRW scattering, compact Higgs transitions, black-hole information, inverse moduli theory and evidence-based capital allocation, each labelled by how far the work has come.

title: Relative metric estimates near reducible Yang–Mills connections
description: A new paper compares surface Yang–Mills quotient metrics and the complete small gauge spectrum with a finite-dimensional model, uniformly across changing stabilizers and arbitrarily separated scales. It includes a leading metric correction and explicit quaternionic comparisons. The manuscript, source and finite calculations are public, with a Zenodo archive.

title: Stability walls and geometric degeneration
description: Three new papers connect realizable toric tangent stability chambers, uniform small Hermitian–Einstein spectra, metric response and actual Hermitian Yang–Mills flow. The Geometry & moduli guide gives geometric and analytic reading routes into the programme. The manuscripts, sources and reproducible finite calculations are public.

title: Small Dolbeault eigenvalues near stability walls
description: A new paper determines every small Hermitian–Einstein endomorphism eigenvalue near intersecting stability walls, with a uniform relative estimate across independent slope gaps. It includes a second-order two-factor expansion and toric examples with arbitrarily many spectral scales. The manuscript and exact matrix computations are public, with a Zenodo archive.

title: Local stability chambers for toric tangent bundles
description: A new paper classifies tangent stability for a family of toric projective bundles, constructs local chambers with arbitrarily many independent boundaries, and determines nearby stable polarizations in the 31 indecomposable semistable census cases. Includes the full manuscript and exact computations.

title: The same law in a black hole and a stock market
description: An interactive essay: the Marchenko–Pastur law, written down in 1967 for neither, governs the noise in a correlation matrix and the radiation of an evaporating black hole.

title: One year per year
description: An interactive essay on alpha discovery when hypotheses are free and the evidence that judges them still arrives at the speed of the calendar.

title: Nobody did it
description: An interactive essay on deterrence when delegating decisions to machines produces acts with no author.

title: Why broken things make invariants
description: An interactive essay on how gauge theory and Floer theory build invariants from the ways their solutions break.

title: Who vouches for a machine?
description: An interactive essay on the trust layer machine commerce still lacks: a court, a ledger, an underwriter, and the prices that would feed them.

title: Two ways for a theory to fail
description: An interactive essay on geometric and informational singularities, from Norton’s dome to the island formula.

title: The balance point of a hexagon
description: An interactive essay on slope stability, Kähler–Einstein metrics, and six arrows that balance on average and still lean.

title: Nothing condenses alone
description: An interactive essay on Higgs transitions in compact Calabi–Yau threefolds, where gravity turns local symmetries into shared constraints.

title: A page for every paper
description: The 39-paper collection now has individual abstract pages, citation downloads, and archive links. Thirty-three papers also have verified PDF copies hosted here.

title: Mirror symmetry for conifold relations
description: The current public manuscript is dated 25 October 2026. The paper page links its abstract, PDF, source, and archived version.
